captions.table1: Reported reproducibility practices, medical versus other papers, nine venue-years. Medical papers had higher reporting rates for nine of ten indicators. Shares among papers with a known value; pooled difference is the Mantel-Haenszel risk difference over venue-years with a 95% paper bootstrap interval.
captions.table2: Unadjusted and adjusted differences in reproduction outcomes of attempted ICML 2026 papers, medical minus other (post hoc analyses, Notes 9-9 to 9-15). Rows marked subsample use the 220 papers with coded claim requirements.
captions.table3: Agreement between reported practices and logbook evidence of material use, 222 attempted ICML 2026 frame papers; the last column pools them with the 300-paper extension sample. Agreement was limited for code and data and higher for weights.
captions.table4: Sensitivity analyses of reported practices, medical minus other, Mantel-Haenszel over venue-years, percentage points with 95% CI (post hoc, Note 9-22): main analysis, papers reporting a training-set size, and all coded papers with unclear treated as no reported release.
captions.tablea1: Papers in the frame and with a coded full text, by group and venue-year. Retrieval was nearly complete where open proceedings exist and lowest at NeurIPS 2026.
